claimed_status: §0a of `docs/plans/native-embedded-suwayomi.md` claims Phase 1 (desktop sidecar) is "built": the Rust supervisor with "brokered loopback port, `server.conf` boot with `kcefEnabled=false`, readiness gate, capped-backoff restart", the "Tauri bundle wiring (`bundle.resources` + jlink-JRE `build-jre.sh` (61 MB) + SHA-verified `fetch-suwayomi-jar.sh` + tightened IPC-only CSP)", and the `native-sidecar.yml` CI matrix. The Gate-C scorecard claims: cold-start <30 s proven, "no orphaned java (proven)", kill->degraded+restart 🟡 (unit-covered only), and a live MangaDex read proven end-to-end via the shimmed-`invoke` harness. Only the "literal DOM `` blob paint" and a real hosted `workSources` response are listed as unverified slivers.
actual_status: The desktop lane is demo-ready, not production-ready. The happy path is genuinely solid and matches the docs: the engine is loopback-only (`server.ip = "127.0.0.1"`, suwayomi.rs:233), JS reaches it only over IPC (`suwayomi_gql`/`suwayomi_image`) with a tight CSP that does not allow the loopback port, the jar SHA-256 is truly verified (not just recorded) in fetch-suwayomi-jar.sh:53-101, the hosted Bearer token is never forwarded to the local engine (composite-backend.ts:185-189), and the desktop page-image byte path touches the Cloudflare Worker at zero points — `img.komiq.cc` in the CSP is dead allowance for Tauri builds. What is missing is everything around the happy path: there is NO pipeline that produces a distributable desktop bundle (nothing runs build-jre.sh/fetch-suwayomi-jar.sh at build time, and no CI job runs `tauri build`), so a real build ships with an empty `jre/` and no jar and a permanently degraded engine; no macOS entitlements/signing for a bundled JVM; abnormal termination orphans the JVM AND leaves a stale lockfile that permanently bricks the engine; quitting the app blocks the UI thread for 6 s whenever the engine never started; the loopback engine has no authentication at all while `suwayomi_gql` forwards arbitrary mutations; and release builds install no logger, so a degraded engine in the field is undiagnosable. "No orphaned java (proven)" is proven only for the clean-shutdown path.

findings.title: Nothing builds/bundles the engine artifacts — a real desktop build ships an empty jre/ and no jar
findings.detail: `beforeBuildCommand` is only `pnpm build` (tauri.conf.json:9-10) — it never runs `scripts/fetch-suwayomi-jar.sh` or `scripts/build-jre.sh`. `.github/workflows/native-sidecar.yml:96-156` builds the JRE and verifies the jar but stops at `cargo test` + `upload-artifact`; no job anywhere runs `tauri build` (the only reference is the manual `desktop:build` script in apps/reader/package.json:16). Both artifact dirs are gitignored (apps/reader/src-tauri/.gitignore: `/jre/*`, `/suwayomi/Suwayomi-Server.jar`), leaving only `jre/.gitkeep`. So the bundle wiring in tauri.linux/macos/windows.conf.json:4-7 copies an empty directory and `resolve_java` (suwayomi.rs:485-502) / `resolve_jar` (505-518) both fail at runtime.
findings.failure_scenario: Fresh clone -> `pnpm desktop:build` -> installer builds green -> user launches the app -> `resolve_config` fails -> `start()` logs 'engine unavailable' and sets Degraded (suwayomi.rs:572-579) -> the native engine never runs and every read silently falls back to the hosted backend, i.e. the entire Phase-1 feature is absent from the shipped product with no build-time error.
findings.fix_sketch: Chain the artifact scripts into `beforeBuildCommand` (or a `tauri build` wrapper script) and add a CI job that runs build-jre.sh + fetch-suwayomi-jar.sh + `tauri build` per desktop target and asserts the produced bundle contains `jre/<slug>/bin/java*` and `suwayomi/Suwayomi-Server.jar`.

findings.title: No macOS entitlements / hardened-runtime / signing config for the bundled JVM
findings.detail: tauri.macos.conf.json contains only `bundle.resources`; a repo-wide grep for `entitlements`, `hardenedRuntime`, `signingIdentity` returns nothing. A jlink'd JRE lands in `Contents/Resources/jre/<slug>/` (resolve_java, suwayomi.rs:491-499), i.e. nested Mach-O executables inside Resources, and HotSpot needs JIT/W^X memory. Under the hardened runtime that Apple requires for notarization, a JVM needs `com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit` (+ typically `allow-unsigned-executable-memory` / `disable-library-validation`), and nested executables outside `Contents/MacOS`/`Frameworks` break `codesign --deep`/notarization.
findings.failure_scenario: Sign + notarize the macOS bundle -> notarization rejects the nested unsigned JRE binaries, or (if stapled anyway) the first `spawn_engine` on a hardened-runtime build is killed by the kernel when HotSpot maps W+X memory -> engine boot fails on every macOS user, restarting forever with a 30 s stall per attempt.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a macOS entitlements plist (allow-jit, allow-unsigned-executable-memory, disable-library-validation), reference it from `bundle.macOS.entitlements`, and either move the JRE under `Contents/Frameworks` or add a signing step that signs every nested Mach-O in the JRE before the outer bundle.

findings.title: Stale lockfile after any abnormal exit permanently disables the engine
findings.detail: `acquire_lock` (suwayomi.rs:539-557) uses `create_new` and writes the PID but never validates the holder's liveness; the file is removed only by `LockGuard::drop` (98-102), which runs solely on a clean process exit. `start()` treats a taken lock as fatal for the session (581-588): it logs, sets Degraded and returns — with no retry, no takeover, and no UI affordance to clear it. The code comment at 535-538 admits this is PARTIAL.
findings.failure_scenario: App is SIGKILLed / the machine loses power / the WebView crashes -> `komika-suwayomi.lock` survives in `<app_data_dir>/suwayomi/` -> every subsequent launch, forever, reports `another Komika instance holds the engine lock` and the engine stays Degraded until the user manually deletes a file inside an OS-specific app-data directory.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the create_new marker with a real advisory lock (`fs2`/`fd-lock`, or an OS file lock) so the OS releases it on process death; failing that, read the stored PID and take over the lock when the PID is not alive (cfg-gated `kill(pid,0)` / `OpenProcess`), and re-arm a takeover attempt on a timer instead of one-shot Degraded.

findings.title: Orphaned `java` survives SIGKILL/logout/crash — kill_on_drop is the only reaping mechanism
findings.detail: The only guarantees that the JVM dies are `kill_on_drop(true)` (suwayomi.rs:272) and the explicit `stop_child` on the shutdown path (360-366), both of which require the Rust process to actually run code. A grep of src-tauri/src for `pdeathsig`/`PDEATHSIG`/`JobObject`/`libc` returns nothing, so there is no parent-death signal on Linux, no Job Object on Windows, and no watchdog on macOS. On Unix the child is simply reparented to init and keeps running. §0a's 'no orphaned java (proven)' is proven only for the clean `stop_child` path (the #[ignore]d test at suwayomi.rs:843-887).
findings.failure_scenario: User force-quits the app / the OS logs out and SIGKILLs it / the WebView process takes the app down -> the 512 MB-heap JVM keeps running, keeps its loopback port and the H2 data dir open, and (combined with the stale lockfile) the next app launch cannot start an engine and cannot see the orphan either. Repeated crashes stack multiple orphaned JVMs.
findings.fix_sketch: cfg-gated hard parent-binding: `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGKILL)` in a `pre_exec` on Linux, a Job Object with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` on Windows, and on macOS a kqueue `NOTE_EXIT` watch on the parent inside the child launcher (or write the child PID next to the lockfile and kill any live, stale PID at startup).

findings.title: Every app quit blocks the UI thread for 6 s when the engine never started
findings.detail: `RunEvent::Exit` does `block_on(sup.stop_and_wait())` on the main thread (lib.rs:272-280). `stop_and_wait` (suwayomi.rs:198-210) polls for `state == Stopped` for a full 6 s. But when `start()` bails early — no JRE/jar resolved (572-579) or lock refused (581-588) — no supervision task exists, so nothing ever sets `Stopped` and the loop always burns the entire 6 s before the backstop transition at 209. That early-bail state is the DEFAULT for any build produced by the current pipeline (see desktop-no-release-bundling-pipeline) and for every `tauri dev` run without a local JRE.
findings.failure_scenario: User quits the desktop app on a build without the bundled engine -> the window disappears but the process hangs on the main thread for 6 s; on Windows/macOS the OS shows a beachball/'not responding', and a second launch during that window hits the still-held lockfile.
findings.fix_sketch: Track whether the supervision task was actually spawned (e.g. an `AtomicBool started` set right before `tauri::async_runtime::spawn(run_supervisor(...))`) and return immediately from `stop_and_wait` when it is false or when the state is already Degraded/Stopped with no task; alternatively have `start()` set `Stopped` instead of `Degraded` on its early-bail paths.

findings.title: Embedded engine runs with no authentication; any local process gets full GraphQL control (arbitrary extension install)
findings.detail: `render_server_conf` (suwayomi.rs:231-241) writes ip/port/webUI/tray/kcef/flareSolverr but enables no authentication, so `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/graphql` is fully open to every process running as (or alongside) the user. Loopback-only binding is not an authorization boundary on a multi-process desktop. The engine's GraphQL surface includes repo/extension mutations — the app itself uses them (local-suwayomi-backend.ts provisioning) — so an unauthenticated caller can point the engine at an arbitrary extension repo and get arbitrary JVM code executed in-process. `suwayomi_gql` (suwayomi.rs:619-641) also forwards any query/mutation verbatim with no allowlist, so the same power is one XSS away inside the WebView.
findings.failure_scenario: Any unprivileged local process scans 127.0.0.1 for a Suwayomi `aboutServer` response, then POSTs `updateExtensionRepos`/`installExternalExtension` pointing at an attacker-hosted jar -> arbitrary code runs inside the Komika-launched JVM with the user's privileges and full access to the app data dir.
findings.fix_sketch: Generate a random per-boot credential, write it into server.conf (the pinned build's auth keys — `server.basicAuth*` / `server.authMode`+`authUsername`/`authPassword`; confirm names against v2.3.2243), attach the matching `Authorization` header in `poll_ready`, `suwayomi_gql`, `suwayomi_image` and `cloudflare::apply_settings`, and add a mutation allowlist (or at least a repo/extension-install denylist) to `suwayomi_gql`.

findings.title: Native reader downloads every page of a chapter before showing page 1
findings.detail: The reader load resolves all pages up front: `await Promise.all(domainPages.map((p) => images.resolvePage(p)))` (source.ts:1833, same at 1855). On web that is a free URL rewrite (image-provider.ts:113-115 -> 70-78), but on desktop `NativeImageProvider.resolvePage` actually pulls the bytes — `/api/…` -> `suwayomi_image` -> loopback engine -> source CDN (image-provider.ts:213-225, 163-166; suwayomi.rs:706-746) — throttled to 6 concurrent fetches by the shared semaphore (lib.rs:40-48). Nothing renders until the LAST page of the chapter has been downloaded through the engine.
findings.failure_scenario: Open a 40-page chapter with the native engine on: the reader route awaits ~40 engine-proxied downloads (~7 sequential batches of 6, each a live source fetch) before the first byte is painted — tens of seconds of blank screen — and a single slow/failing page stalls the whole chapter instead of one image.
findings.fix_sketch: Make the native provider lazy: hand the reader page descriptors and resolve bytes per-page on demand (or resolve only the first N and prefetch the rest in the background), keeping the existing blob-revoke logic in routes/read/[slug]/+page.svelte:104-112.

findings.title: Readiness gate never observes child exit — a JVM that dies instantly still burns the full 30 s timeout
findings.detail: `boot_engine` (suwayomi.rs:339-356) spawns the child then awaits `poll_ready` only; it never `select!`s on `child.wait()`. A JVM that exits in under a second (corrupt/incompatible jar, wrong JRE module set, port stolen, OOM) is not noticed, so every failed attempt costs the whole `READY_TIMEOUT` (31) and reports the misleading 'engine did not become ready within 30s' instead of the child's exit status — while the real stderr is discarded in release builds (see desktop-no-release-logging). It also breaks the restart-storm accounting: each cycle takes >=30 s + backoff, so the `>5 restarts in 60 s` window (42, 437-453) can never trip for boot failures and the app retries a hopeless boot indefinitely.
findings.failure_scenario: Ship a JRE whose module set is missing a class Suwayomi needs -> JVM throws and exits in ~1 s -> supervisor waits 30 s, reports a timeout error, sleeps 2 s, repeats forever, with no exit-status diagnostic anywhere and no storm cap ever engaging.
findings.fix_sketch: In `boot_engine`, `tokio::select!` the `poll_ready` future against `child.wait()`; on early exit return an error carrying the exit status (and the last N captured stderr lines), and count consecutive boot failures separately from the 60 s crash window.

findings.title: Shutdown SIGKILLs the JVM with no SIGTERM, so H2 is never closed cleanly
findings.detail: `stop_child` (suwayomi.rs:360-366) calls `child.start_kill()`, which is SIGKILL on Unix / TerminateProcess on Windows — the JVM's shutdown hooks never run, on every single quit. The same happens on the mid-boot stop path, which just `break`s and relies on `kill_on_drop` (398-402, 272). Per §0a the engine's embedded DB is H2, which relies on shutdown hooks to close its store and lock files cleanly.
findings.failure_scenario: Normal quit -> JVM killed mid-write -> next launch H2 must recover, or refuses with 'Database may be already in use'/locked-file errors -> boot fails, and because boot failure is only visible as a 30 s readiness timeout the user sees an engine that is silently degraded after a routine restart.
findings.fix_sketch: Send a graceful signal first: on unix `libc::kill(child.id(), SIGTERM)` (or the engine's own shutdown mutation over the existing loopback client), wait the existing `GRACE` window, and only then `start_kill()`; keep the current behaviour on Windows.

findings.title: The JVM and the Cloudflare loopback listener start for every desktop user even when the native-engine flag is off
findings.detail: `run()`'s setup unconditionally manages the supervisor and calls `suwayomi::start(...)` (lib.rs:255-256); `start()` in turn always launches the loopback Cloudflare shim listener (suwayomi.rs:594-597) and spawns the supervision loop (599). The feature gate is frontend-only (`PUBLIC_KOMIKA_NATIVE_ENGINE`, apps/reader/src/lib/config.ts:60, default `off` per apps/reader/.env:19) and is never communicated to Rust. The comment at 559-562 asserts 'an unused engine is harmless'.
findings.failure_scenario: A shipped desktop build with the flag off still spawns a `-Xmx512m` JVM at every launch, writes/refreshes an H2 data dir, holds a lockfile, binds a second loopback listener for the CF shim, and burns cold-start CPU — all for a subsystem no code path uses; on a laptop this is battery/RAM cost plus two extra local attack surfaces per the auth finding.
findings.fix_sketch: Make the engine lazily started: expose a `suwayomi_start` command (or read a `KOMIKA_NATIVE_ENGINE` compile-time/env value in Rust) and have `context.ts` invoke it only when `config.nativeEngine && isTauri()`; keep `start()`'s current body behind that trigger.

findings.title: Release builds install no logger, so all engine diagnostics are read and discarded
findings.detail: `tauri_plugin_log` is registered only inside `if cfg!(debug_assertions)` (lib.rs:241-247). The supervisor's stdout/stderr pumps (suwayomi.rs:278-293) faithfully read every JVM line and hand it to `log::info!`/`log::warn!` targeted at `suwayomi`, where in a release build it goes nowhere. Same for every `log::error!` on boot failure (428) and the restart/storm transitions (445-448).
findings.failure_scenario: A user's engine is stuck Degraded in production. The only signal available is `suwayomi_status.lastError`, which for the dominant failure mode says exactly 'engine did not become ready within 30s' (suwayomi.rs:327-331) — the JVM's actual stack trace was read from the pipe and dropped. The bug is undiagnosable without asking the user to run a debug build.
findings.fix_sketch: Register `tauri_plugin_log` unconditionally with a rotating file target (Info in release, Debug in dev) so the `suwayomi` target lands on disk; additionally retain the last N stderr lines in the supervisor and attach them to `lastError` on boot failure.

findings.title: The bundled JRE is unpinned and unverified — only the jar is a real supply-chain pin
findings.detail: build-jre.sh only checks that `${JAVA_HOME}/bin/jlink` is executable (18-24); it asserts no JDK version, vendor or checksum despite the header claiming 'Requires JDK 21', and it records no digest of its output. CI feeds it `actions/setup-java` with `java-version: '21'` (.github/workflows/native-sidecar.yml:76-80), i.e. a floating Temurin patch release. Contrast with suwayomi/VERSION:4-6 + fetch-suwayomi-jar.sh:53-101, where the jar hash is genuinely enforced. So half the shipped runtime (the half that executes the other half) is reproducible only by luck.
findings.failure_scenario: A runner (or a maintainer's laptop with `JAVA_HOME` pointing at JDK 17 or 24) produces a JRE whose module set/class files differ from the one the `MODULES` list at build-jre.sh:57 was validated against -> the bundle boots on the builder's machine but the module set is subtly wrong for the pinned jar, and nothing in the pipeline detects the drift because no digest is recorded or compared.
findings.fix_sketch: Assert `"${JAVA_HOME}/bin/java" -version` reports the pinned feature+vendor (fail otherwise), pin the exact Temurin version in the workflow, and emit/record a manifest digest of the jlink output (e.g. sorted `sha256sum` over the tree) into `suwayomi/VERSION`-style pin file that CI re-verifies.

findings.title: `KOMIKA_JAVA_BIN`/`KOMIKA_SUWAYOMI_JAR` are honoured in release builds and the bundled artifacts are never re-verified at launch
findings.detail: `resolve_java` (suwayomi.rs:485-502) returns any path from `KOMIKA_JAVA_BIN` before probing the bundle, and `resolve_jar` (505-518) does the same with `KOMIKA_SUWAYOMI_JAR`; neither is gated on `cfg!(debug_assertions)`. Neither path re-checks the artifact against the SHA-256 pin that fetch-suwayomi-jar.sh enforced at build time (suwayomi/VERSION:5), so the bundled jar is trusted purely on location.
findings.failure_scenario: A per-user install (Linux tarball/AppImage extraction, Windows per-user install dir) or any process able to set the app's environment (a user LaunchAgent/.desktop wrapper, a systemd user unit) points `KOMIKA_JAVA_BIN` at an arbitrary executable or swaps the on-disk jar -> Komika launches attacker-controlled code as the user with no integrity check and no warning.
findings.fix_sketch: Gate both env overrides behind `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` (or a `KOMIKA_DEV_ENGINE=1` opt-in), and verify the bundled jar's SHA-256 against a digest compiled in via `env!`/`include_str!` from suwayomi/VERSION on first boot (cache the result keyed on mtime+len to keep restarts cheap).

findings.title: The deterministic native checks and the chapter-list smoke never run in CI
findings.detail: native-sidecar.yml:134-146 documents that the chapter-list rung is 'DELIBERATELY NOT IMPLEMENTED' and asserts nothing. The deterministic checks under apps/reader/src-tauri/e2e/{native-read,fallback-ladder,offline-queue} are referenced by no workflow (grep over .github/ finds only the repo-root Playwright `e2e/` job in ci.yml:169-218). So the only automated desktop gate is `cargo clippy`, `cargo test --lib`, and the `aboutServer` boot smoke (native-sidecar.yml:116-132) — the composite/fallback/reconciliation logic §0a calls 'proven' is proven by manual runs only.
findings.failure_scenario: A refactor in composite-backend.ts's D7 reconciliation or in the fallback ladder breaks native reads; every CI gate stays green because the checks that would catch it are run by hand, and the regression is only found on a device.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a CI job that runs the ladder + offline-queue checks (they are network-free) on every PR, and wire native-read behind a manual/nightly job that already has the jar+JRE artifacts from the sidecar matrix.

findings.title: Spawning `java.exe` from a GUI app on Windows pops a console window
findings.detail: `spawn_engine` (suwayomi.rs:257-276) builds a plain `tokio::process::Command` with piped stdio and `kill_on_drop`, with no `#[cfg(windows)] .creation_flags(CREATE_NO_WINDOW)` (grep for `creation_flags` in src-tauri/src returns nothing) and no use of `javaw.exe`; `java_exe()` (469-475) deliberately picks the console launcher `java.exe`. A Windows GUI-subsystem process spawning a console-subsystem child allocates a new console.
findings.failure_scenario: On Windows the app launches and a black console window appears next to the app window (and again on every supervised restart), staying for the JVM's lifetime — visually broken product behaviour and, with the restart loop, a flurry of windows during a boot-failure storm.
findings.fix_sketch: Under `#[cfg(windows)]` use `std::os::windows::process::CommandExt::creation_flags(0x08000000 /* CREATE_NO_WINDOW */)` on the command (and/or prefer `javaw.exe` when present).

findings.title: Brokered port is released before the JVM binds it — a racing process makes the boot fail as an opaque 30 s timeout
findings.detail: `broker_port` (suwayomi.rs:220-225) binds 127.0.0.1:0, reads the port and immediately drops the listener; the port then sits unowned for the whole `prepare_data_dir` + `spawn` + JVM-startup window (344-347), seconds during which any other process can claim it. `poll_ready` (299-334) treats every non-conforming response as 'not ready yet' and cannot tell 'engine still booting' from 'a foreign service owns this port'.
findings.failure_scenario: Another app (or a second Komika data dir) grabs the ephemeral port between the broker and the JVM bind -> the JVM fails to bind and exits, but the supervisor polls a stranger's HTTP service for 30 s and reports 'engine did not become ready within 30s', then retries with the same class of failure.
findings.fix_sketch: Detect the collision instead of guessing: pair the child-exit `select!` from desktop-boot-ignores-child-exit with a re-broker on failure, and/or verify the readiness response really is Suwayomi (already checks `data.aboutServer.version`) before declaring the port ours — plus log the child's bind error.

findings.title: Desktop CSP still allows img.komiq.cc and dev localhost origins that the native build never uses
findings.detail: The Tauri CSP allows `https://img.komiq.cc` in both `img-src` and `connect-src`, plus `http://localhost:8080` and `ws://localhost:5173` (tauri.conf.json:25). Under Tauri, `createImageProvider` always returns `NativeImageProvider` (image-provider.ts:240-242), which never constructs a Worker URL — `workerBaseUrl` is read only by `WebImageProvider.resolve` (image-provider.ts:76) — and the SPA build never server-renders (apps/reader/src/routes/+layout.ts:11-12), so no Worker URL can be baked into the HTML either. The Worker allowance is therefore dead, and the two localhost entries are dev-only.
findings.failure_scenario: No functional failure today; the cost is that the CSP no longer documents the real dependency set, and it silently keeps a path open for a future regression that reintroduces Worker URLs on desktop (exactly the dependency the product goal forbids) without any gate noticing.
findings.fix_sketch: Drop `https://img.komiq.cc` from both directives in the desktop CSP (keep it only in the web/Cloudflare build's headers) and move the `localhost:8080` / `ws://localhost:5173` entries into a dev-only config override.

findings.title: Self-hosted/LAN Suwayomi backend on desktop shows no images: fetch_image blocks private addresses
findings.detail: `is_blocked_ip` (lib.rs:170-217) rejects loopback/private/CGNAT targets for every `fetch_image` call, and the native provider routes non-engine absolute URLs through `fetch_image` (image-provider.ts:204-206, 222-224). But with `PUBLIC_KOMIKA_BACKEND_KIND=suwayomi` (apps/reader/src/lib/config.ts) the adapter absolutises page URLs against the user's own server base (packages/api/src/suwayomi-backend.ts:431), which is typically `http://192.168.x.x:4567` or `http://localhost:4567`.
findings.failure_scenario: A desktop user configures Komika against their own LAN Suwayomi -> every page and cover request is rejected by the SSRF guard with 'host resolves to a non-public address' -> a fully blank reader, with the error visible only in a debug build's console.
findings.fix_sketch: Pass the configured backend origin down to Rust (a managed allowlist set at startup) and exempt exactly that origin (host+port) from `is_blocked_ip`, leaving the guard intact for arbitrary third-party source URLs.

claimed_status: The task framing (and commit 86578ab, "feat(ios): N4.2 in-process Zero-JVM engine launcher — signed engine .ipa builds [N4.2]") claims iOS is implemented and only blocked on a physical-device test: an in-process Zero JVM booted via JNI_CreateJavaVM, "gql/image command bodies verbatim from desktop", "desktop build/clippy/test 20/0 · ios+sim clippy clean · sim build green (stub)", with only "on-device boot NOT yet run". The n4-ios-spike claims Cloudflare "ports directly" to iOS via WKHTTPCookieStore, and n4.1-ios-jvm-findings.md §6 step 5 lists iOS lifecycle tie-in as part of N4.2.
actual_status: The module is a plausible, carefully-commented first cut, and the cfg aliasing is genuinely correct for every real iOS triple (verified with `rustc --print cfg`: aarch64-apple-ios-sim and x86_64-apple-ios both report target_abi="sim" → stub; aarch64-apple-ios reports abi="" → device module). findings.title: suwayomi_ios.rs is compiled by no CI job; its unit tests never run anywhere
findings.detail: The module is gated to `all(target_os="ios", not(target_abi="sim"))` (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:20-22), so it is NOT compiled by any host-target build. native-sidecar.yml's only job has a 4-entry desktop matrix (:48-64) and runs `cargo clippy --all-targets` (:116) and `cargo test --lib` (:120) on the host triple — neither ever selects an iOS target. There is no `cargo check --target aarch64-apple-ios` step in the repo. Consequently the 843-line module's own tests (suwayomi_ios.rs:747-843: server.conf template, image-path guard, 4 port-retry tests) are dead code that has never executed, and the file's only type-check is the one manual run recorded in commit 86578ab ("ios+sim clippy clean"). Note also that docs/plans/n4-ios-build-attempt.md:40 claims "`cargo check --target aarch64-apple-ios-sim` is clean" as evidence the native crate compiles for iOS — that target compiles suwayomi_mobile.rs (the stub), not this module, so it proves nothing about it.
findings.failure_scenario: Any later refactor of lib.rs's shared surface (e.g. renaming `crate::image_fetch_semaphore`, changing `tauri::ipc::Response`, bumping tauri/jni-sys) compiles green on every CI runner and every developer machine while silently breaking the iOS device build; the breakage is discovered only when someone with a Mac + iPhone attempts a release build. Equally, a regression in `validate_image_path` (the SSRF guard) on the iOS copy would ship unnoticed because its tests are never run.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a `macos-14` job to native-sidecar.yml that installs the `aarch64-apple-ios` target and runs `cargo clippy --target aarch64-apple-ios --all-targets -- -D warnings` plus `cargo clippy --target aarch64-apple-ios-sim`. To make the module's unit tests actually run, hoist the target-independent pure logic (render_server_conf, validate_image_path, percent_decode_once, acquire_boot_port) into a small `suwayomi_shared` module compiled on all targets so `cargo test --lib` covers it on Linux.

findings.title: run_jvm exits the VM-owning thread while still attached to the JVM on every post-create error path
findings.detail: `JNI_CreateJavaVM` (suwayomi_ios.rs:403-409) attaches the calling thread as the VM's primordial Java thread. After that point, five paths `return Err(..)` without ever calling `DetachCurrentThread` or `DestroyJavaVM`: :427 (FindClass MainKt), :435 (GetStaticMethodID), :442 (FindClass java/lang/String), :447 (NewObjectArray), :456 (main threw). The Err propagates to the closure at :577-582, the closure returns, and the spawned `suwayomi-jvm` thread (:573-576) exits. The JNI spec requires an attached native thread to detach before exiting; HotSpot does not auto-detach, so the JavaThread keeps a pointer to a stack region the pthread has just unmapped. The VM itself is left running (non-daemon Java threads may already exist) with a dangling primordial thread and no owner. This is also the only path where a *terminal* degrade is reported, so it is exactly the state the engine ends in when the classpath/jar is wrong — i.e. the most likely first-run failure on a real device.
findings.failure_scenario: Bundle regression drops Suwayomi-Server.jar from the classpath (or the jar's Main-Class differs from the hardcoded `suwayomi/tachidesk/MainKt` at :423): FindClass returns null, run_jvm returns Err at :427, the attached thread exits, and the still-live VM's next safepoint/GC stack-scan walks the freed stack → SIGSEGV in a JVM thread, which on iOS is an app crash rather than the intended clean `degraded` + hosted fallback.
findings.fix_sketch: Restructure run_jvm so the post-create body is a closure whose result is handled by a single cleanup epilogue that calls `((**vm).DetachCurrentThread.unwrap())(vm)` (and logs) before returning Err; on the success path keep DestroyJavaVM. Wrap the closure in `std::panic::catch_unwind` for the same reason.

findings.title: No Cloudflare bypass exists on iOS — the N-CF shim is compiled out and flareSolverr is hard-disabled
findings.detail: `mod cloudflare` is `#[cfg(desktop)]` (lib.rs:16-17), so the FlareSolverr-v1 loopback shim and WebView solver do not exist in an iOS binary. suwayomi_ios.rs's `render_server_conf` writes `server.flareSolverrEnabled = false` (:293) and, unlike the desktop supervisor (suwayomi.rs:590-594 starts the shim, :408-413 points the engine at it via `setSettings` on every Ready), the iOS `start()` (:513-614) never starts a shim and never calls `apply_settings`. The plan's iOS spike asserts the opposite is easy — n4-ios-spike.md Q4: "WKHTTPCookieStore works ... so the shim can harvest cf_clearance ... N-CF ports" — but nothing is implemented, and the desktop solver could not be reused as-is anyway (it is built on `tauri::webview::WebviewWindowBuilder`, cloudflare.rs:35, i.e. a second desktop window).
findings.failure_scenario: A user on iOS opens a chapter from any Cloudflare-gated source (a large fraction of Keiyoushi extensions): the embedded engine's CloudflareInterceptor sees 403/`Server: cloudflare`, has no flareSolverrUrl, and returns an error; CompositeBackend.canonicalChapters catches it and permanently memoizes the work in `localUnusable` for the session (composite-backend.ts:403-406), so the device silently reverts to server-fetched content — the exact 'reliance on our hosted fetch path' the native lane is meant to eliminate.
findings.fix_sketch: Either (a) build an iOS solver: a `#[cfg(target_os="ios")]` shim reusing cloudflare.rs's `handle_v1`/`CfShim` (which are WebView-agnostic) with a WKWebView + WKHTTPCookieStore solver behind the `CloudflareSolver` trait, then flip `server.flareSolverrEnabled = true` and call `apply_settings`; or (b) state plainly in §0a and the module docs that CF-gated sources are unsupported on iOS and always fall back to hosted.

findings.title: The entire iOS link recipe lives in a gitignored, hand-edited gen/apple/project.yml with no tracked template
findings.detail: build.rs:20-40 documents that the 13 dlsym-only JDK static libs (libjava, libnio, libnet, libzip, libjimage, …) CANNOT be bundled by cargo and must be `-Wl,-force_load`ed from `gen/apple/project.yml`, together with `-lz -liconv -lc++`, the CoreFoundation/Foundation frameworks, `DEAD_CODE_STRIPPING=false`, and the `jvm-runtime/lib` folder reference that puts the jimage at the bundle root. `gen/` is gitignored (.gitignore:13) and `git ls-files | grep project.yml` returns nothing — there is no template, no generator, and no CI. The only guard is stage-ios-jvm-runtime.sh:60-75, which greps the generated file for three substrings (`jvm-runtime/lib`, `force_load`, `CoreFoundation.framework`) and can neither restore them nor verify the other required settings (dead-code stripping, the per-lib force_load list, the system libs).
findings.failure_scenario: A developer (or a future release job) runs `pnpm exec tauri ios init` to regenerate gen/apple. The app still links — `JNI_CreateJavaVM` is bundled into libapp.a by build.rs — but the dlsym-only `Java_*`/`JNI_OnLoad_*` members of libjava/libnio/libzip are dropped, so `JNI_CreateJavaVM` fails during java.base bootstrap (or the VM aborts) on device, producing an unexplained permanent `degraded`. If the developer skips stage-ios-jvm-runtime.sh, `check_bundled_runtime` (:493-508) at least degrades cleanly, but the force_load loss has no such guard.
findings.fix_sketch: Track a `src-tauri/ios/project.yml.patch` (or a full templated project.yml plus a `scripts/apply-ios-project.sh` that re-applies it idempotently after `tauri ios init`), and extend stage-ios-jvm-runtime.sh to assert every required setting (each of the 13 force_load entries, DEAD_CODE_STRIPPING=false, -lz/-liconv/-lc++) rather than three substrings.

findings.title: Zero iOS lifecycle/jetsam handling; the only shutdown hook is a RunEvent iOS never delivers
findings.detail: n4.1-ios-jvm-findings.md:302 lists "Tie to iOS lifecycle (applicationWillResignActive/DidEnterBackground → pause/checkpoint; foreground → resume), per N4.2" as a required N4.2 step. suwayomi_ios.rs contains no lifecycle code at all: no background/foreground observer, no memory-warning handler, no heap trim, no request quiescing, no checkpointing. The only shutdown path is lib.rs:272-280's `RunEvent::Exit` → `stop_and_wait`, which on iOS is effectively dead code (suspended apps are SIGKILLed; Exit is not delivered). Combined with `boot_attempted` (:522) making a second in-process boot impossible, the module has no answer for the single most common iOS runtime event. The module docstring (:35-42) acknowledges the limits as "deliberate for this gate, N4.8 refines", which is honest — but it means the lane is not production-ready, contrary to the 'device-test-blocked' framing.
findings.failure_scenario: User backgrounds the app mid-chapter while `suwayomi_image` requests are in flight. iOS suspends the process; the reqwest calls hold 60 s timeouts (HTTP_TIMEOUT, :66) against a frozen loopback server. On foreground the sockets are dead, the pending IPC promises reject, and — because status is still `ready` — CompositeBackend retries against the engine and memoizes works as `localUnusable`. If instead iOS jetsams the app (169 MB runtime + 174 MB jar + 256 MB heap + up to 6×32 MiB image buffers), the user sees a silent cold restart with no diagnostic.
findings.fix_sketch: Subscribe to Tauri's mobile lifecycle/`RunEvent` equivalents (or add a small Swift plugin) to: on background, mark state `stopped` and cancel in-flight engine IPC; on memory warning, drop caches and call the VM's `System.gc` via a retained JavaVM handle; on foreground, re-verify the engine with a short `aboutServer` probe and flip back to `ready` (or `degraded` with the restart hint). Store the `*mut JavaVM` in the supervisor so a foreground probe/attach is possible at all.

findings.title: -Xss1m contradicts the module's own Zero-stack reasoning and applies to every engine worker thread
findings.detail: The module gives its own VM thread a 16 MiB native stack precisely because "the Zero interpreter burns C stack per Java frame, so give it far more than -Xss" (:69-71, JVM_THREAD_STACK). It then passes `-Xss1m` (:379), which is at or below the HotSpot default and applies to every thread the JVM creates itself — i.e. all of Suwayomi's Javalin/OkHttp/Kotlin-coroutine workers, the extension installer (dex2jar), and the class loaders that actually run deep recursive Java code under the interpreter. Under Zero every Java frame consumes a C frame of the bytecode interpreter, so 1 MiB buys a fraction of the Java depth it buys on a JIT VM. Desktop's JIT sidecar sets no -Xss at all (suwayomi.rs:259-266).
findings.failure_scenario: First MangaDex extension install on device: dex2jar / the ASM class-writer recursion runs on a Javalin worker with a 1 MiB Zero stack and throws StackOverflowError. The engine returns a GraphQL error, `refFor` throws, and CompositeBackend memoizes every affected work as `localUnusable` — the on-device engine appears to 'work' (status ready) but never serves a chapter.
findings.fix_sketch: Either drop `-Xss1m` (let the VM default apply) or raise it to a Zero-appropriate value (e.g. `-Xss4m`/`-Xss8m`) and record the measured peak thread count so the RSS impact is bounded deliberately rather than by accident; add a note that this value is an N4.3 measurement input.

findings.title: No -Djava.io.tmpdir / -Duser.home passed; the JVM's defaults are not sandbox-writable on iOS
findings.detail: The option list (:371-383) sets only class.path, the Suwayomi rootDir, headless, -Xmx and -Xss. On a desktop Unix JVM `java.io.tmpdir` defaults to `/tmp` and `user.home` to the passwd entry; inside the iOS app sandbox `/tmp` is not writable and the passwd home (`/var/mobile`) is not app-writable — the writable temp dir is the container's own `tmp/`. Whether the pinned openjdk/mobile tree derives these from `confstr(_CS_DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR)` under `__IOS__` is unverified anywhere in the repo (n4.1-ios-jvm-findings.md §7 explicitly lists on-device boot as unproven), and the data-dir code (`prepare_data_dir`, :298-306) only guarantees the Suwayomi rootDir. Pinning both properties is a one-line, zero-risk removal of an unverified dependency.
findings.failure_scenario: Suwayomi's extension installer downloads the MangaDex APK/jar and calls `File.createTempFile` (or H2/OkHttp create a temp/spill file); with `java.io.tmpdir=/tmp` the write throws `IOException: Read-only file system`, extension provisioning fails permanently, and every work is memoized `localUnusable` — engine reports `ready` while serving nothing.
findings.fix_sketch: In run_jvm, add `-Djava.io.tmpdir=<data_dir>/tmp` (created by prepare_data_dir) and `-Duser.home=<app_data_dir>`, and extend prepare_data_dir to `create_dir_all` that tmp dir.

findings.title: No liveness check after Ready — a dead in-process engine still reports state "ready" forever
findings.detail: Once `poll_ready` succeeds the readiness task ends (:592-613) and nothing ever re-checks the engine. Desktop supervises the JVM continuously (`suwayomi.rs:421` `status = child.wait()` → transitions to Degraded), but the in-process VM has no observable exit: if the engine's HTTP server dies (OutOfMemoryError under the 256 MB heap, an uncaught error in a Javalin thread, or a Zero StackOverflowError), `Inner.state` stays `Ready` and `base_url`/`ready_endpoint` keep handing out the dead port. JS `isReady()` (local-suwayomi-backend.ts:117-118) therefore keeps returning true.
findings.failure_scenario: The engine OOMs mid-session under -Xmx256m (desktop uses 512m, suwayomi.rs:261). Every subsequent `suwayomi_gql` returns a connection-refused string; CompositeBackend catches each one and adds the work to `localUnusable` (composite-backend.ts:403-406), so the entire session silently and permanently degrades to hosted content while `suwayomi_status` still reports `ready` and `lastError: null` — no signal to the user, the logs, or the runbook.
findings.fix_sketch: Spawn a low-frequency (e.g. 30 s) `aboutServer` heartbeat after set_ready; on N consecutive failures call `degrade("engine stopped responding")` so the UI/ladder sees the terminal state and stops paying the per-work failure cost.

findings.title: iOS bundle contents/size are unverified: the 218 MB desktop-JRE leak has no in-repo guard and the real payload is ~340 MB
findings.detail: n4-ios-build-attempt.md:26-30 records the 218 MB .ipa caused by the desktop jar+JRE being baked into the Xcode resource-copy phase at first `tauri ios init`, explicitly noting the `resources` override does not fix an already-generated project. The only in-repo remedy is tauri.ios.conf.json narrowing resources to `suwayomi/Suwayomi-Server.jar` — which is inert unless gen/apple was regenerated after it existed, and gen/apple is gitignored with no verification step. Meanwhile the intended iOS payload is itself unbounded: a 174 MB jar (per apps/reader/src-tauri/.gitignore:7) plus the ~169 MB jre-ios runtime (n4.1-ios-jvm-findings.md §5), and no script enforces a ceiling — in contrast to the desktop path, where scripts/build-jre.sh has a 150 MB hard ceiling enforced in CI (native-sidecar.yml:96-107).
findings.failure_scenario: Someone regenerates gen/apple on a machine whose jre/ was populated by build-jre.sh; the iOS copy phase re-includes `jre/aarch64-macos` (macOS mach-o binaries), producing an oversized .ipa that either fails codesign or ships 62 MB of unusable macOS executables — the exact failure already observed once, with nothing in the repo to catch a recurrence.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a `scripts/verify-ios-bundle.sh` invoked after `tauri ios build` that asserts the .app contains `assets/suwayomi/Suwayomi-Server.jar` and `lib/lib/modules`, contains NO `assets/jre/`, and is under an explicit size ceiling; call it from stage-ios-jvm-runtime.sh's checks and from any future iOS CI job. Separately, trim the jimage with a Suwayomi-tailored `--add-modules` set (already flagged in n4.1-ios-jvm-findings.md §5).

findings.title: The plan of record's §0a never mentions N4.2; committed device-only code has no recorded status or verification
findings.detail: `grep -n "N4" docs/plans/native-embedded-suwayomi.md` returns only :85 and :95, both describing the N4 *spike*; §0a still reads "Remaining after Wave E spikes: ... review the spikes and green-light the N4 gating prototype". Yet 843 lines of device-only Rust, the build.rs link path, two scripts, a C++ shim and a vendored patch are committed (86578ab). The code's own docs assert unexercised claims as verified fact — suwayomi_ios.rs:12-27 ("verified against the pinned openjdk/mobile sources") and :421-422 ("Manifest Main-Class ... verified from META-INF/MANIFEST.MF") — while n4.1-ios-jvm-findings.md §7 correctly says on-device boot is unproven, and N4.3 (cold-start/RSS go/no-go, n4-ios-spike.md:262) has never been run. There is no honest single place a reader can learn that iOS ships an engine that has never booted.
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer or future agent reads §0a, concludes iOS has no engine implementation (or conversely reads the commit message and concludes it works), and either duplicates the work or enables PUBLIC_KOMIKA_NATIVE_ENGINE for an iOS build whose engine has never been observed to reach `ready` on hardware.
findings.fix_sketch: Add an N4.2 entry to §0a stating exactly what landed, what is unbuilt (CF, lifecycle, N4.3 measurements), and the standing `could_not_verify` (no device boot); downgrade the 'verified' language in suwayomi_ios.rs:12-27/:421-422 to 'derived from sources, unverified on device'.

findings.title: Only -Xmx is capped; metaspace, direct buffers and code cache are unbounded in a jetsam-limited process
findings.detail: `-Xmx256m` (:378) bounds only the Java heap. Metaspace (large: Kotlin + Suwayomi + every dynamically converted extension classloader), NIO direct buffers used by OkHttp/Netty for image streaming, and per-thread stacks are all outside it, and none of `-XX:MaxMetaspaceSize`, `-XX:MaxDirectMemorySize`, `-XX:+UseSerialGC` or a thread-count bound is set. On top of that the Rust side allows 6 concurrent 32 MiB image buffers (lib.rs:40, and suwayomi_ios.rs:713-716 shares the same pool) plus the ~149 MB jimage mapping. The plan's R4 risk ("Memory on 4 GB devices ... safe with -Xmx256m") is therefore only half-implemented, and N4.3's RSS gate has never been measured.
findings.failure_scenario: A prefetch burst of 6 large pages (192 MB native) coincides with extension class loading (metaspace growth) and OkHttp direct buffers; total RSS crosses the foreground jetsam ceiling on a 4 GB iPhone and the OS kills the app mid-read, with no crash report attributable to the engine.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `-XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=128m -XX:MaxDirectMemorySize=64m -XX:+UseSerialGC` to the option list, and consider lowering MAX_CONCURRENT_IMAGE_FETCHES on iOS (a `#[cfg(target_os="ios")]` constant in lib.rs) so the native buffer ceiling is ~64 MB rather than 192 MB.

findings.title: Mac Catalyst (target_abi="macabi") resolves to the device JNI module and the device JVM link
findings.detail: Verified with `rustc --print cfg`: aarch64-apple-ios-macabi reports `target_os="ios", target_abi="macabi"`. lib.rs:20 selects suwayomi_ios.rs for any iOS triple that is not `sim`, and build.rs:47-50 applies the same `abi != "sim"` test before linking the device-only `jre-ios/aarch64-ios` static libs. Catalyst is not a current target, so this is latent, not live — the two simulator triples (aarch64-apple-ios-sim and x86_64-apple-ios, both abi="sim") and the device triple (aarch64-apple-ios, abi="") all resolve correctly.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone adds a Mac Catalyst build: cargo pulls in the in-process JNI module and build.rs feeds it iOS-device .a files, so the link fails with mach-o platform mismatches (or, worse, appears to link and aborts at JNI_CreateJavaVM) instead of falling back to the mobile stub.
findings.fix_sketch: Change the two conditions to an explicit allowlist of the device ABI, e.g. `all(target_os = "ios", target_abi = "")` in lib.rs and `target_abi.is_empty()` in build.rs, so any future Apple ABI defaults to the stub.

findings.title: Cargo.toml pins rust-version 1.77.2 but lib.rs uses cfg(target_abi), stabilized in 1.78
findings.detail: `rust-version = "1.77.2"` (Cargo.toml:9) while lib.rs:20/25 use `target_abi = "sim"` in `cfg`. `cfg(target_abi)` was feature-gated (`cfg_target_abi`) until Rust 1.78; on a 1.77 toolchain the gated cfg name is an E0658 error, not a silently-false predicate. Cargo.toml:41-42 also comments that "cargo target cfg tables can't express target_abi reliably across toolchains" — the same caveat applies to the source cfgs and is not reflected in the MSRV.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor (or a distro/CI image) pinned to the declared MSRV 1.77.2 gets a hard compile error on lib.rs:20 for every target, including the desktop build that has nothing to do with iOS.
findings.fix_sketch: Bump `rust-version` to at least 1.78 (the crate already builds with 1.95 here) and note the target_abi requirement next to the cfg block.

findings.title: Engine boot prologue (fs writes + up to 600 ms of sleeps) runs on the iOS main thread in setup()
findings.detail: `suwayomi::start` is called from Tauri's `.setup()` hook (lib.rs:255-256), which runs on the main (UI) thread. Before spawning the JVM thread it does `current_exe` + `exists` checks (:493-508), resource resolution, `create_dir_all` + `write` of server.conf (:298-305), and — on a contended-port retry — up to four `std::thread::sleep(150 ms)` calls (:546) on that same thread. Only the JVM creation itself is moved off-main (:573-583).
findings.failure_scenario: On a cold launch where the ephemeral port is repeatedly stolen, the iOS main thread blocks ~600 ms plus filesystem latency during app initialization, delaying first paint and, in the worst case (slow container I/O plus retries), contributing to the UIApplication launch watchdog budget.
findings.fix_sketch: Move the whole `boot()` closure (:530-550) into the spawned thread (or a `tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking`) and have it publish the degrade via the supervisor, leaving `start()` as a pure spawn.

findings.title: A panic in the JVM thread closure records no degrade; status sits at "starting" for the full 300 s budget
findings.detail: The spawned closure (:576-583) has no `catch_unwind`. Any panic inside it — e.g. `CString::new(..).expect("jvm option contains NUL")` (:382), or the `.unwrap()`s on the JNI function pointers at :424/:432/:439/:444/:452 if a fn pointer is null in a mis-linked VM — kills the thread without calling `sup_jvm.degrade`. The supervisor then reports `starting` until `poll_ready`'s 300 s READY_TIMEOUT (:62) finally degrades it. (Panicking through JNI frames is not a risk here since no Rust code is invoked from Java.)
findings.failure_scenario: A mis-staged runtime leaves `(**env).FindClass` null; the closure panics; the UI shows the engine as `starting` for five minutes with no error, then a generic "engine did not become ready within 300s" instead of the real cause, which was only printed to the device console.
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap the closure body in `std::panic::catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(..))` and `degrade("engine thread panicked")` on Err; replace the JNI fn-pointer `.unwrap()`s with null checks that return a descriptive Err.

findings.title: Android has no embedded engine at all: suwayomi_mobile.rs is a total stub and zero Android-specific native code exists
findings.detail: `start()` is a single log line (`suwayomi_mobile.rs:69-71`); `suwayomi_status` returns a hard-coded `state:"degraded"` (`:84-91`); `suwayomi_gql` and `suwayomi_image` return a constant `Err` (`:95-112`); `SuwayomiSupervisor` is a unit struct with an empty `stop_and_wait` (`:50-59`). `lib.rs:23-28` binds Android to this module. A repo-wide grep of `apps/reader/src-tauri/src/` and `Cargo.toml` finds ZERO occurrences of `target_os = "android"`, `dlopen`, `jniLibs`, `CookieManager`, or `Service` — none of N3.2 (JNI_CreateJavaVM launcher), N3.3 (foreground service + supervisor mapping), N3.4 (loopback/network_security_config), N3.6 (CF WebView bridge), N3.8 (packaging) or N3.9 (compliance) from `docs/plans/n3-android-spike.md:260-334` exists. `jni-sys` is declared only under `[target.'cfg(target_os = "ios")'.dependencies]` (`Cargo.toml:41-42`), so Android could not even reference the JNI ABI today.
findings.failure_scenario: Install any Android build: `suwayomi::start()` logs and returns; `LocalSuwayomiBackend.isReady()` sees `degraded` → false; `CompositeBackend.localReady()` false; every chapter list and page URL comes from the hosted MangaDex mirror. Any work whose only source mapping is a non-MangaDex Keiyoushi source has no `canonicalPages` path at all and the reader shows an empty chapter/page state — the on-device-fetch product promise is entirely absent on Android.
findings.fix_sketch: Land N3.2 first: an `#[cfg(target_os = "android")]` engine module that `dlopen`s the bundled `libjvm.so` from `nativeLibraryDir` and `dlsym`s `JNI_CreateJavaVM` (Android cannot use iOS's static-link trick), reusing the iOS supervisor state machine, port broker and readiness gate. Then N3.3 (Kotlin foreground service owning VM lifetime) and N3.4 (network_security_config for 127.0.0.1). Requires an Android SDK/NDK host.

findings.title: No Android JVM artifact, no jar bundling, no gen/android — an Android build today would ship neither a JVM nor the engine jar
findings.detail: Base `bundle.resources` is `[]` (`tauri.conf.json:31`). The per-OS overrides that actually bundle the engine exist only for desktop and iOS (`tauri.linux.conf.json` → `["suwayomi/", "jre/"]`, `tauri.ios.conf.json` → `["suwayomi/Suwayomi-Server.jar"]`); there is **no** `tauri.android.conf.json`, so an Android bundle would carry no `Suwayomi-Server.jar`. `bundle.android` (`tauri.conf.json:39-41`) sets only `debugApplicationIdSuffix` — no `minSdkVersion` (spike §Q5 requires 26–29 for the exec/dlopen model) and no ABI filter (spike requires arm64-v8a-only). `scripts/` contains no Android JDK builder: `build-jre.sh:27-40` derives its slug from `uname -m`/`uname -s` and only accepts macos/linux/windows, and `build-ios-jvm.sh` is Xcode/iOS-only. `gen/android` has never been generated (`/.gitignore:13`; `gen/` holds only `schemas/`). N3.1's own acceptance text (`n3-android-spike.md:262-266`) demands "a documented, size-budgeted arm64 JDK artifact; a script that `jlink`s it reproducibly" — that artifact and script do not exist.
findings.failure_scenario: Run `tauri android build` on a machine with the Android SDK/NDK: the APK contains no `libjvm.so` in `jniLibs/arm64-v8a` and no `Suwayomi-Server.jar` in assets, so even after N3.2 lands the launcher would fail at `dlopen`/classpath resolution. With no ABI filter, Gradle also emits an armeabi-v7a slice for which no JVM was ever built.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `tauri.android.conf.json` bundling `suwayomi/Suwayomi-Server.jar` as an asset; add `scripts/build-jdk-android.sh` that produces a 16 KB-page-aligned arm64-v8a OpenJDK (GPLv2+CE) staged into `gen/android/app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a` with `extractNativeLibs=true`; pin `minSdkVersion` and `ndk.abiFilters = ['arm64-v8a']` in the generated Gradle config; extend `.gitignore` for the new vendored dir.

findings.title: android-jdk-probe validates the one execution model Android forbids (execve of a `java` launcher on glibc), not the in-process JNI model the plan depends on
findings.detail: The probe's entire runtime is `docker run --platform linux/arm64 eclipse-temurin:21 java -verbose:class … -jar /engine/Suwayomi-Server.jar` (`run.sh:34-35` and `:128-135`). That is (a) a **glibc** Linux userland, not bionic; (b) started by **exec'ing the `java` launcher binary** — precisely the model `n3-android-spike.md:158-166` says the API-29 W^X/exec ban rules out; (c) never calls `JNI_CreateJavaVM`, which is N3.2's stated acceptance (`n3-android-spike.md:268-274`: "one process, no `execve`"). It therefore transfers only the architecture-independent claim "the jar's bytecode + the pure-Java dex2jar/H2/Exposed path run on an aarch64 JDK 21". Everything Android-specific is untested by it: bionic `dlopen` of a bundled `libjvm.so`, ART coexistence, the foreground-service requirement, `nativeLibraryDir` exec legality, Android storage paths / `rootDir` under app-private storage, 16 KB page size on Android 15+, Doze/background process death, and JIT-vs-Zero behaviour on device. `FINDINGS.md` nonetheless opens with "Two findings materially *de-risk* Android beyond the plan's assumptions", and `native-embedded-suwayomi.md` §0a folds it into the Android status line.
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer reads §0a's "N3.1 headless acceptance PASS (11/11)" and green-lights N3.2 believing the runtime is de-risked; the first real Android attempt then hits an entirely unexercised class of failures (bionic/libjvm.so linkage — spike risk R8; foreground-service lifetime — R9; 16 KB page alignment), i.e. all remaining Android risk is still 100% live despite a green probe.
findings.fix_sketch: Retitle the probe and its FINDINGS/§0a prose to exactly what it proves ("stock v2.3.2243 bytecode + dex2jar + H2 run on a stock GPL+CE aarch64 JDK 21 under glibc, launched by execve") and add an explicit 'does NOT cover' list (bionic, JNI_CreateJavaVM, foreground service, storage paths, 16 KB pages, ART coexistence). Keep the de-risking claim scoped to the H2/no-native-DB and dex2jar findings only.

findings.title: §0a records "N3.1 headless acceptance PASS" although two of N3.1's three acceptance clauses (jlink'd arm64 JDK artifact, GraalJS init) were never satisfied
findings.detail: `n3-android-spike.md:262-267` defines N3.1 as: (i) "a documented, size-budgeted arm64 JDK artifact; a script that `jlink`s it reproducibly", and (ii) a headless boot that "Proves GraphQL API + dex2jar + Exposed/SQLite + **GraalJS init** on a stock JDK". Neither holds. (i) No Android jlink script exists — `scripts/` has only `build-jre.sh` (host-slug-only, `build-jre.sh:27-40`) and `build-ios-jvm.sh`; the probe used the stock 300+ MB `eclipse-temurin:21` container image with no module trimming or size budget at all. (ii) `e2e/android-jdk-probe/FINDINGS.md` (GraalJS section) states plainly: "the **Truffle polyglot `Context` is lazily created on first JS eval** … 0 `com.oracle.truffle`/`org.graalvm.polyglot` class-loads here (expected)" — GraalJS was never initialised, so JS-dependent Keiyoushi sources are entirely unproven. Despite this, `native-embedded-suwayomi.md` §0a states "**N3.1 headless acceptance PASS** (11/11, cold-start 3–4 s)" and `n3-android-spike.md:373-380` §4a repeats it.
findings.failure_scenario: Planning proceeds to N3.2 on the assumption N3.1 is closed. The unmeasured items then surface late: the arm64 JDK footprint (the dominant term in the ~120–180 MB APK estimate, spike §Q5) is still unknown, and the first JS-heavy source hits an untested GraalJS/Truffle init on a bundled Android JDK — spike risk R4, which the probe explicitly did not retire.
findings.fix_sketch: Downgrade §0a and §4a to "N3.1 PARTIAL": list the 11 assertions that did pass, and carry forward two open items — (a) build + size-budget a jlink'd arm64 Android JDK, (b) force a GraalJS eval (a JS-using source, or a direct `JavaScriptEngine.evaluate` probe) and record init cost + jar footprint.

findings.title: No Cloudflare capability on Android: the shim is desktop-gated and fetch_image carries no cookie jar or per-source headers
findings.detail: `lib.rs:16-17` gates the whole FlareSolverr shim behind `#[cfg(desktop)]`, so `cloudflare.rs` is compiled out on Android; `suwayomi_mobile.rs:69-71` starts nothing, so no `setSettings(flareSolverrUrl=…)` wiring ever runs. There is no Kotlin Tauri plugin exposing `android.webkit.CookieManager` (`grep CookieManager` over the crate: zero hits), which `n3-android-spike.md:196-211` identifies as mandatory because Tauri-Android's own cookie API returns empty. The only image path Android has is `fetch_image`, which sets a single static UA (`lib.rs:65`) and a same-origin `Referer` (`lib.rs:69-76`) and attaches no cookies — `reqwest::Client` is rebuilt per request (`lib.rs:105-108`) with no cookie store at all. Note the user's stated goal is Worker-free image fetch on Android, and a CF-gated CDN is exactly where the Worker is currently doing the work for web.
findings.failure_scenario: A Keiyoushi source (or a MangaDex mirror) behind a Cloudflare managed challenge returns 403/503 to `fetch_image`; `lib.rs:130-132` turns it into `Err("upstream returned 403 Forbidden")`, `Cover.svelte`'s `.catch` sets `broken`, and after 2 retries the user sees a permanent grey placeholder. There is no solve path, no cookie replay, and (on native) no Worker fallback, so the page simply never loads.
findings.fix_sketch: Un-gate `cloudflare.rs` for Android (replacing the desktop WebView solver behind a trait), add a Kotlin `@TauriPlugin` exposing `solve(url)`/`getCookie(url)`/`userAgent()` over `android.webkit.CookieManager` + a WebView, and thread the harvested `{cf_clearance, UA}` into the shim; UA-unify WebView ↔ shim ↔ engine OkHttp. Interim mitigation: give `fetch_image` an optional cookie/header map so a solved clearance can be replayed even before the engine lands.

findings.title: suwayomi_ios.rs has no shared abstraction — Android would duplicate ~600 lines of supervisor/transport code verbatim
findings.detail: `lib.rs:16-28` selects exactly ONE `suwayomi` module per target via `#[path]` aliasing; there is no trait, no `engine_core` module, and no shared crate. Yet roughly 500 of `suwayomi_ios.rs`'s 843 lines are entirely platform-neutral: the supervisor + state machine (`:109-215`), `broker_port`/`port_is_bindable`/`acquire_boot_port` (`:220-278`), `render_server_conf`/`prepare_data_dir` (`:285-306`), `poll_ready` (`:310-344`), `validate_image_path`/`percent_decode_once` (`:658-703`) and the four IPC commands (`:619-843`). The genuinely iOS-only surface is small and precisely identifiable: (a) `JNI_CreateJavaVM` resolved as a **statically linked** symbol (`Cargo.toml:41-42` + `build.rs:76-83`) — Android must instead `dlopen("libjvm.so")` from `nativeLibraryDir` and `dlsym`; (b) `check_bundled_runtime` (`:493-508`), which encodes iOS's `<exe dir>/lib` java.home derivation — irrelevant on Android; (c) `-Xmx256m` jetsam cap and `JVM_THREAD_STACK` sized for the Zero interpreter (`:70-71, :377-380`) — Android has JIT and a different memory regime; (d) the one-boot-per-process / no-DestroyJavaVM policy (`:36-44`, `:206-210`), which on Android should become a foreground-service restart. Nothing in the module is generic over these, so an Android module written today is a copy-paste fork that will drift.
findings.failure_scenario: N3.2 is implemented as `suwayomi_android.rs` copied from `suwayomi_ios.rs`. A later fix to the shared logic (e.g. the `acquire_boot_port` TOCTOU handling at `:238-247`, or the `validate_image_path` traversal guard at `:658-703`) is applied to one file and silently missed in the other — a security-relevant divergence in the image-path validator across two shipping platforms.
findings.fix_sketch: Before N3.2, extract a `suwayomi_core.rs` holding `Status`/`EngineState`/`Inner`/supervisor, the port broker + retry, `render_server_conf`/`prepare_data_dir`, `poll_ready`, `validate_image_path`, and the gql/image proxy bodies; leave a small per-OS `boot_vm()` (static-symbol on iOS, `dlopen`/`dlsym` on Android) and `resolve_runtime()` behind a trait or two `cfg` fns. `suwayomi_ios.rs` then shrinks to ~250 lines and Android reuses the rest.

findings.title: The android-jdk-probe is a one-shot manual artifact — it is not in any workflow, so an engine-pin bump cannot regress it
findings.detail: `native-sidecar.yml:47-60` defines a four-entry desktop matrix (aarch64-macos, x86_64-macos, x86_64-linux, x86_64-windows) and no step in the file references `e2e/` at all; `ci.yml`'s only `e2e/` mentions (`:167`, `:218`) are the reader Playwright suite, not `src-tauri/e2e/`. The probe additionally needs a live Docker daemon able to run `linux/arm64` (`run.sh:74-79` skips otherwise), network egress to Keiyoushi/GitHub/MangaDex, and the gitignored 174 MB jar (`src-tauri/.gitignore` excludes `/suwayomi/Suwayomi-Server.jar`). The spike's own mitigation for risk R6 (upstream drift) is "we pin; **re-run N3.1/N3.5 probes on each bump**" (`n3-android-spike.md:348`) — there is no mechanism to do so.
findings.failure_scenario: `suwayomi/VERSION` is bumped past v2.3.2243 and the new build switches the default store to sqlite-jdbc or bumps GraalJS. CI stays green (the desktop matrix boots via the jlink'd JRE and never checks the DB engine or Truffle), the Android premises silently invert (N3.5 stops being moot, a native `.so` becomes mandatory), and nobody learns until an Android build is attempted months later.
findings.fix_sketch: Add an `android-premises` job to `native-sidecar.yml` on `ubuntu-24.04-arm` (or QEMU) that runs `fetch-suwayomi-jar.sh` then a network-free subset of `run.sh`: assert the jar SHA matches VERSION, assert `META-INF/services/java.sql.Driver` still lists only postgresql+h2 (H2 premise), and boot to `aboutServer`. Skip the extension-store assertions that need egress.

findings.title: fetch_image's SSRF guard makes every self-hosted/LAN backend's covers and pages unloadable on Android with no fallback
findings.detail: `validate_image_url` rejects any host resolving to a private, loopback, link-local or CGNAT address (`lib.rs:142-165`, `is_blocked_ip` `:170-217`). On native, `NativeImageProvider.resolve` sends own-origin assets to `fetch_image` after prefixing `apiOrigin` (`image-provider.ts:218-221`) and sends every absolute non-MangaDex URL there too (`:222-224`) — and unlike the web provider it never honours `config.direct` (`image-provider.ts:66-72` is `WebImageProvider`-only). So a Komika API or a `backendKind='suwayomi'` server on `192.168.x.x`/`10.x`/`localhost` — the documented self-host and dev configurations — has every cover and page rejected before a request is sent. Android is the platform where LAN self-hosting is most common (and where there is no Worker fallback, since `WebImageProvider` is unreachable inside Tauri per `image-provider.ts:240-242`).
findings.failure_scenario: User points an Android build at a self-hosted Komika at `http://192.168.1.20:8080`. Catalogue metadata loads fine over GraphQL (that goes through `fetch`, not the guard), but `images.resolveCover('/covers/ab/cd.webp')` → `fetch_image('http://192.168.1.20:8080/covers/ab/cd.webp')` → `Err("host resolves to a non-public address: 192.168.1.20")` → `Cover.svelte:113-117` catches and sets `broken`. Every cover in the app is a grey placeholder and every reader page fails, with the reason visible only in native logs.
findings.fix_sketch: Exempt the configured backend origin(s) from the guard: pass `apiOrigin` / `suwayomiUrl` down as an allowlist (or add a `fetch_own_asset` command that only accepts URLs under the configured API origin) so first-party self-hosted hosts bypass `is_blocked_ip` while third-party source URLs keep the full SSRF check.

findings.title: The native CSP still allow-lists the Cloudflare Worker and two dev origins that no native build ever uses
findings.detail: `tauri.conf.json:25` sets `img-src 'self' blob: data: https://img.komiq.cc` and `connect-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost http://localhost:8080 https://api.komiq.cc https://img.komiq.cc ws://localhost:5173`. Inside Tauri, `createImageProvider` always returns `NativeImageProvider` (`image-provider.ts:240-242`) and every byte arrives over IPC as a blob (`:165-180`), so `https://img.komiq.cc` is dead allowance in both directives — and its presence is what makes the audit premise "Android falls back to the Worker" look plausible on inspection. `http://localhost:8080` and `ws://localhost:5173` are dev-server conveniences; on Android loopback is shared across the device, so any co-installed app that binds tcp:8080 becomes a permitted `connect-src` destination for the WebView.
findings.failure_scenario: A hostile or merely buggy app on the same Android device binds 127.0.0.1:8080; injected or compromised frontend script can then reach it (and exfiltrate to it) within the CSP, which would otherwise have blocked the destination. No exploit chain is claimed — this is unnecessary attack surface shipped in the production native CSP.
findings.fix_sketch: Drop `https://img.komiq.cc` from both `img-src` and `connect-src` in `tauri.conf.json`, and move `http://localhost:8080` / `ws://localhost:5173` into a dev-only config override so the shipped mobile/desktop CSP is `connect-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost https://api.komiq.cc`.

findings.title: isReady() issues an IPC round-trip per content call for an answer that is a compile-time constant on Android
findings.detail: `isReady()` dynamically imports `@tauri-apps/api/core` and `invoke('suwayomi_status')` on every call with no memoization (`local-suwayomi-backend.ts:113-122`). `CompositeBackend.localReady()` wraps it unmemoized (`composite-backend.ts:168-169`) and is called from `canonicalChapters` (`:352`) and `canonicalPages` (`:421`). On Android the Rust side answers from a hard-coded literal (`suwayomi_mobile.rs:84-91`) — the same `degraded` forever — so each of those is a guaranteed-useless serialize/IPC/deserialize hop on the reader's hot path. The existing `localUnusable` memo (`composite-backend.ts:352`) only short-circuits provisioning, not the readiness probe.
findings.failure_scenario: Opening a 37-page chapter on Android: `canonicalChapters` + `canonicalPages` each pay an IPC round-trip whose result is statically known to be false, adding latency to the first paint of every chapter open on the platform where the answer can never change within a process lifetime.

actual_status: The Worker claim is TRUE and structurally enforced: `createImageProvider` returns `NativeImageProvider` on any Tauri build (`image-provider.ts:241`) and that class never reads `workerBaseUrl` — there is no code path from a native build to `img.komiq.cc`. But "no Worker" is not "no hosted proxy": in production the server hands out absolute `https://api.komiq.cc/api/v1/manga/{id}/thumbnail` and `/api/v1/manga/{m}/chapter/{c}/page/{p}` URLs (`apps/server/src/suwayomi.rs:344-350` + `SUWAYOMI_PUBLIC_URL`), and `NativeImageProvider` routes those to `fetch_image` — so every Suwayomi-sourced cover and page on desktop/iOS/Android is still fetched from our origin. The embedded-engine byte path (`/api/…`→`suwayomi_image`) is unreachable in any shipped build: `PUBLIC_KOMIKA_NATIVE_ENGINE=off` in `.env` and is not overridden by `.env.production`, which is what `beforeBuildCommand: "pnpm build"` loads. Even with the flag on it only fires for MangaDex-spine works, because `CompositeBackend.pages()` always delegates to hosted (`composite-backend.ts:244-248`). Beyond routing, the byte path is not production-hardened: the reader eagerly `Promise.all`s EVERY page of a chapter through `resolvePage` (`source.ts:1833,1855`), so on native one failed page collapses the whole chapter to "No pages available" and a whole chapter's bytes are held in memory before first paint; `fetch_image` has no Content-Type validation, no retry, no per-source header channel; its SSRF guard blocks the app's own API origin whenever that origin is loopback/LAN (breaking `tauri dev` and every self-hosted deploy); and the native CSP omits `api.komiq.cc` from `img-src`, blocking avatars and comment media.
