findings.title: A single failed page image collapses the entire chapter to "No pages available" on native
findings.detail: `const urls = await Promise.all(domainPages.map((p) => images.resolvePage(p)))` (source.ts:1833 and again at 1855) runs inside `live(fn, emptyReader(seriesId))` (source.ts:43-51), which swallows ANY throw and returns the empty reader view. On web `WebImageProvider.resolvePage` is a pure string rewrite that cannot reject (image-provider.ts:113-115), so this is safe. On native `NativeImageProvider.resolvePage` awaits a Rust `invoke` that rejects on any non-2xx, timeout, DNS failure, size-cap trip, or SSRF-guard rejection (lib.rs:109-133). `Promise.all` rejects on the first such page, so ONE 502/403/slow page destroys the whole chapter. The reader's per-page retry (`retryImage`, routes/read/[slug]/+page.svelte:257-260) cannot help: it only remounts an `` around an already-resolved blob URL, and in this failure mode no URL was ever produced.
findings.failure_scenario: User opens a 40-page chapter on desktop/iOS. Page 17's CDN returns 502 (or the hosted /api/v1/... proxy answers 502 from `serve_suwayomi_image`, apps/server/src/main.rs:612-616). `fetch_image` returns Err("upstream returned 502"), `Promise.all` rejects, `live()` catches and returns `emptyReader`. The user sees "No pages available" for a chapter where 39/40 pages were fine, and refreshing re-runs the same all-or-nothing fetch.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace `Promise.all` with `Promise.allSettled` and map rejections to a null/empty `url` so the reader renders a per-page error tile (the `pageError`/`retryImage` UI already exists at routes/read/[slug]/+page.svelte:243-260); make `retryImage` re-invoke `images.resolvePage(page)` for that index instead of only remounting the ``.

findings.title: Native reader downloads every page of a chapter into memory before first paint
findings.detail: The same `Promise.all(domainPages.map(resolvePage))` at source.ts:1833/1855 is the ONLY page-resolution site — there is no windowed prefetch anywhere. On native each element is a full Rust `invoke` returning the whole image as an ArrayBuffer over IPC, wrapped in a Blob and retained for the chapter's lifetime by the revoke effect (routes/read/[slug]/+page.svelte:98-113). The Rust semaphore (`MAX_CONCURRENT_IMAGE_FETCHES = 6`, lib.rs:40-48) bounds only IN-FLIGHT buffers, not the retained total, and it is shared with `suwayomi_image` and with every cover on screen — so opening a chapter also starves cover loading for the duration. `loading="lazy"` on the `` tags is useless here because the bytes were already pulled.
findings.failure_scenario: A 200-page webtoon chapter at ~1.5 MB/page on an iPhone: ~300 MB of Blob-backed bytes plus 200 IPC transfers must complete before the reader paints page 1. In the same process the in-process Zero JVM already runs under -Xmx256m (suwayomi_ios.rs:68 note), so jetsam kills the app; on desktop the user stares at a blank reader for tens of seconds. With a 30 s per-hop timeout and 6 permits, a slow source makes time-to-first-page = ceil(200/6) x latency.
findings.fix_sketch: Resolve only the first N pages (e.g. 3) in `load`, return the raw `Page[]` alongside, and have the reader component resolve/release a sliding window around the current index; release blobs that fall out of the window via `images.release`.

findings.title: fetch_image's SSRF guard blocks the app's own API origin, breaking every image in `tauri dev` and LAN self-hosts
findings.detail: `NativeImageProvider.resolve` sends own-origin assets through `fetch_image`: `/covers/…` and `/avatars/…` are prefixed with `apiOrigin` (image-provider.ts:218-221) and absolute hosted proxy URLs fall through to `resolveViaLocalProxy` -> `fetch_image` (image-provider.ts:204-206, 222-224). `validate_image_url` then rejects any host resolving to a non-public address (lib.rs:159-161 with the predicate at lib.rs:170-217), which includes 127.0.0.1 and RFC1918. The dev build's `PUBLIC_KOMIKA_API=http://localhost:8080/graphql` (apps/reader/.env:15) and the Docker self-host default `http://${PUBLIC_HOST:-localhost}:${SERVER_PORT:-8080}` (deploy/docker-compose.yml:186) both land squarely in the blocked set. There is no exemption for the configured API origin anywhere in the Rust side.
findings.failure_scenario: Developer runs `pnpm desktop:dev`. Every cover calls fetch_image("http://localhost:8080/covers/x.webp") -> Err("host resolves to a non-public address: 127.0.0.1") -> Cover.svelte sets `broken` and shows a grey placeholder for the whole app. A self-hoster whose server is at http://192.168.1.20:8080 gets the identical total image blackout in the shipped desktop app, plus (per the finding above) "No pages available" for every chapter.
findings.fix_sketch: Plumb the configured API origin host into Rust (a `tauri.conf.json` value, a `setup`-time `manage`d String, or a dedicated `komika_asset(path)` command that only ever fetches `<configured origin><path>`) and exempt exactly that host:port from `is_blocked_ip` — mirroring the deliberate narrow loopback exemption already used by `suwayomi_image`/`validate_image_path` (suwayomi.rs:643-670).

findings.title: Native CSP omits the API origin from img-src, so avatars and comment media never render in the app
findings.detail: The Tauri CSP is `img-src 'self' blob: data: https://img.komiq.cc` (tauri.conf.json:25) — it whitelists the Worker (which native never uses) but NOT `https://api.komiq.cc` or `http://localhost:8080`. Meanwhile `avatarSrc`/`apiAssetSrc` return raw `apiOrigin + '/avatars/…'` strings (apps/reader/src/lib/config.ts:91-95) that go straight into `` in Avatar.svelte:48, and comment attachments do the same via `apiAssetSrc(c.mediaUrl)` (lib/data/social-repo.ts:163) rendered at CommentThread.svelte:359. These bypass the `images` provider entirely, so they are never converted to blobs and are hard-blocked by CSP in every native build.
findings.failure_scenario: Signed-in user opens any comment thread or review in the desktop/iOS app: every avatar and every attached comment image is refused by the renderer ("Refused to load the image … violates Content Security Policy"), falling back to initials/broken tiles. Web is unaffected because the web CSP is not this one.
findings.fix_sketch: Either add the API origin(s) to `img-src` in tauri.conf.json (and the dev localhost origin for `tauri dev`), or — better for the no-remote-origin posture — route avatar/comment media through `images.resolveCover` so they become blob: URLs like every other native image.

findings.title: fetch_image has no channel for per-source Referer/User-Agent/cookies, so the direct path will 403 on real non-MangaDex sources
findings.detail: `image_client_builder()` hardcodes `User-Agent: Komika/0.1 (+https://komika.app)` (lib.rs:65) and `referer_for()` always emits the TARGET's own origin (lib.rs:69-76) — never the source site's series/chapter page. The command signature is `fetch_image(url: String)` (lib.rs:90) with no headers parameter, and the `Page` type carries only `{index, sourceUrl, width, height}` (packages/types/src/index.ts:587-592), so there is no way to convey what a Suwayomi extension would have sent. The design intent (plan §8, and image-provider.ts:139-147) is that non-MangaDex sources go through the engine so "the extension's request context is applied inside the engine" — but that engine path is off in shipped builds and absent entirely on Android/iOS-sim (suwayomi_mobile.rs:104-112), so those sources hit `resolveViaLocalProxy` -> `fetch_image` with generic headers. The Worker is also strictly better here: it at least sends `Accept: image/*,*/*;q=0.8` (apps/worker/src/index.ts, fetchFollowingRedirects), which native omits.
findings.failure_scenario: Android build (engine stub) reading a chapter from any hotlink-protected scanlation source: the page URLs are absolute CDN URLs, `fetch_image` requests them with `Referer: https://<cdn-host>/` and a Komika UA, the CDN returns 403, and (per imagefetch-one-page-failure-empties-chapter) the chapter renders as "No pages available". Today this is masked only because hosted `pages()` returns api.komiq.cc proxy URLs — i.e. the direct native path is untested against real sources.
findings.fix_sketch: Add an optional `headers: HashMap<String,String>` argument to `fetch_image` (allowlisted to Referer/User-Agent/Cookie/Accept), extend `Page` with an optional `headers` field, and have the backends populate it from the source record; keep the engine path as the preferred route when available.

findings.title: Native builds still fetch all Suwayomi-sourced covers and pages from the hosted /api/v1/... proxy
findings.detail: The goal is zero reliance on hosted image serving, not just zero Worker. In production the server rewrites every Suwayomi cover/page URL to `https://api.komiq.cc/api/v1/manga/…` (`SuwayomiClient::abs`, apps/server/src/suwayomi.rs:344-350, driven by SUWAYOMI_PUBLIC_URL; served publicly by `serve_suwayomi_image`, apps/server/src/main.rs:584-620). `NativeImageProvider.resolve` classifies those as neither an engine path (they are absolute, not `/api/`-rooted) nor MangaDex, so they take `resolveViaLocalProxy` -> `fetch_image` -> our origin (image-provider.ts:204-206, 222-224). Three compounding reasons this is the DEFAULT native path, not a fallback: (1) `PUBLIC_KOMIKA_NATIVE_ENGINE=off` in .env:19 with no override in .env.production, and tauri.conf.json:9 builds with `pnpm build`; (2) `CompositeBackend.pages()` is unconditionally hosted (composite-backend.ts:244-248); (3) even `canonicalPages` only engages when the reader chose the MangaDex spine (`spine = resolved.selected.suwayomiMangaId === null`, apps/reader/src/lib/data/source.ts:1791). There is also a latent discriminator collision: if `SUWAYOMI_PUBLIC_URL` is ever unset to empty the server emits RELATIVE `/api/v1/manga/…` paths, which `isEnginePath` (image-provider.ts:182-184) would misroute into the embedded engine with hosted integer ids.
findings.failure_scenario: User installs the shipped desktop/Android app and reads any Suwayomi-sourced series with the server offline (or self-hosts with the server on a laptop that sleeps): every cover and every page 502s or times out, because the 'native' client is proxying its bytes through our origin exactly like the web build. The engine-backed `/api/…`->`suwayomi_image` byte path proven in Gate C never executes.
findings.fix_sketch: Flip the native default on per platform once the engine is device-verified, make `CompositeBackend.pages()` consult the engine the way `canonicalPages` does, and replace the `startsWith('/api/')` discriminator with an explicit tag on `Page` (e.g. `origin: 'engine' | 'cdn' | 'hosted'`) so hosted relative paths can never be mistaken for engine paths.

findings.title: Native fetch_image accepts any Content-Type and produces a MIME-less Blob, unlike the Worker
findings.detail: `fetch_image` checks only `status.is_success()` (lib.rs:130-133) and hands the raw bytes to `read_capped`. The Worker, by contrast, hard-rejects a non-`image/*` upstream (`isImageContentType`, apps/worker/src/index.ts) precisely to stop content laundering (its own I3 note). The JS side then does `new Blob([bytes])` with no `type` (image-provider.ts:170, 177), so even the real Content-Type the server DID send (apps/server/src/main.rs:612, `raw_image_response(content_type, bytes)`) is discarded and the renderer must sniff. Same gap in `suwayomi_image` (suwayomi.rs:726-745, suwayomi_ios.rs:725-742).
findings.failure_scenario: A source CDN returns a 200 HTML interstitial (rate-limit/captcha page) instead of an image. Native buffers up to 32 MiB of HTML, hands it to the DOM as a typeless blob, the `` fails to decode, `onError` fires, and the user sees a generic broken-page tile with no diagnostic — while the identical request on web would have surfaced a clean 502 'Upstream is not an image'.
findings.fix_sketch: Reject non-`image/*` Content-Type in `fetch_image`/`suwayomi_image` (mirroring apps/worker/src/index.ts), and return the Content-Type alongside the bytes so the JS can do `new Blob([bytes], { type })`.

findings.title: In-flight native cover fetches that settle after unmount leak their object URL forever
findings.detail: Cover.svelte's native branch calls `images.resolveCover(source)` and only assigns the result when `alive` is still true (Cover.svelte:112-119). The teardown releases `resolved` (Cover.svelte:120-123), but `NativeImageProvider.resolveCover` has ALREADY called `URL.createObjectURL` inside `toBlobUrl` (image-provider.ts:168-172) by the time the promise settles. If the component unmounted or `src` changed first, `alive` is false, the URL is never stored, and `release()` (image-provider.ts:235-237) is never reachable for it. Object URLs are pinned to the document, so the bytes stay resident for the app session.
findings.failure_scenario: User scroll-flings a discovery grid on iOS. Dozens of `Cover` components mount, kick off a `fetch_image`, and unmount before the (semaphore-queued, up to 30 s) fetch returns. Each late-settling fetch leaks one blob of the full cover bytes. A few minutes of browsing pins tens/hundreds of MB in a jetsam-limited process that also hosts a 256 MB-heap JVM.
findings.fix_sketch: In the `.then`, revoke immediately when `!alive` (`images.release?.(u)`) instead of silently dropping it; equivalently have the provider accept an AbortSignal.

findings.title: Pinning to addrs[0] removes IPv4 fallback, so a broken-IPv6 network fails every native image fetch
findings.detail: `validate_image_url` validates every resolved address but returns only `addrs[0]` (lib.rs:162-164), and `fetch_image` pins the client to that single socket address via `.resolve(&host, addr)` (lib.rs:105-108). reqwest then dials exactly that one IP with no fallback to the other resolved addresses. `lookup_host` returns getaddrinfo order, which under RFC 6724 puts AAAA first whenever the device has a global IPv6 address — a very common state on mobile carriers and captive/hotel Wi-Fi where IPv6 is advertised but not routable. Each failed attempt burns the full 30 s `FETCH_TIMEOUT` (lib.rs:31) while holding one of only 6 semaphore permits (lib.rs:40).
findings.failure_scenario: iPhone on a carrier that hands out a broken IPv6 prefix. Every `fetch_image` pins the AAAA record, hangs 30 s, and errors — so covers all go grey and every chapter reports "No pages available", while Safari on the same phone loads the identical CDN fine via Happy Eyeballs.
findings.fix_sketch: Use `ClientBuilder::resolve_to_addrs(&host, &addrs)` with the full validated list instead of `.resolve(&host, addrs[0])` — this keeps the rebinding defence (only vetted IPs are dialable) while restoring multi-address fallback. Also add an explicit `.connect_timeout(...)` shorter than the total budget.

findings.title: IPv6-literal image URLs never reach the SSRF guard (bracketed host_str breaks DNS lookup), and the test asserting otherwise passes for the wrong reason
findings.detail: `validate_image_url` does `let host = url.host_str()` (lib.rs:148) then `tokio::net::lookup_host((host, port))` (lib.rs:152). For an IPv6-literal URL the `url` crate serializes the host WITH brackets — `Display for Host::Ipv6` writes '[' + addr + ']' (url-2.5.8/src/host.rs:192-194) and `host_start..host_end` spans that serialization (url-2.5.8/src/parser.rs:857-861) — so `host_str()` returns "[::1]", which neither parses as an `IpAddr` nor resolves as a name. Every IPv6-literal URL therefore errors at 'dns lookup failed' and `is_blocked_ip` is never consulted. The behaviour is fail-CLOSED so it is not an SSRF hole, but the test `rejects_loopback_and_lan_literals` (lib.rs:353, `http://[::1]/x.png`) is a false positive: it proves the DNS step failed, not that the v6 guard works, and it will keep passing if the v6 predicate is ever broken.
findings.failure_scenario: A source whose page URLs use a bare IPv6 literal (rare on CDNs but legal, and possible for a self-hosted Suwayomi reachable only over IPv6) is unfetchable on native with the misleading error 'dns lookup failed: …'. Separately, any future regression in the `::a.b.c.d` / v4-mapped folding at lib.rs:191-206 would go undetected because no test actually exercises the guard through `validate_image_url` for a v6 literal.
findings.fix_sketch: Strip surrounding brackets before lookup (`host.trim_start_matches('[').trim_end_matches(']')`), or match on `url.host()` and handle `Host::Ipv6(addr)` directly by calling `is_blocked_ip` without a DNS round-trip; then assert the error message distinguishes 'non-public address' from 'dns lookup failed' in the test.

findings.title: No retry/backoff on the native byte path, and nothing anywhere logs that native is using the hosted proxy instead of the engine
findings.detail: `fetch_image` issues exactly one request per hop and surfaces the first error (lib.rs:109-133); `suwayomi_image` likewise (suwayomi.rs:721-745). `NativeImageProvider` contains zero logging — no counterpart to `WebImageProvider.warnIfProxyRequired` (image-provider.ts:96-111) — so there is no signal at all distinguishing 'bytes came from the embedded engine' from 'bytes came from api.komiq.cc'. `CompositeBackend` warns only on local-path failures (composite-backend.ts:426), and `nativeEngine`/`imgDirect` are build-time `$env/static/public` constants (apps/reader/src/lib/config.ts:53,60) with no runtime override or settings UI, so a user cannot see or change which path they are on. Worst case on latency: the redirect loop is `0..=MAX_REDIRECTS` = 6 requests x 30 s = 180 s while holding 1 of 6 permits.
findings.failure_scenario: Product ships 'native, no proxy' and it silently regresses: a bad `.env.production`, a degraded engine, or a source that only resolves hosted-side sends 100% of image traffic back through api.komiq.cc, and neither the user nor the team sees anything — the app looks identical. Separately, a single transient DNS blip on one page (no retry) becomes an empty chapter.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a bounded jittered retry (2 attempts) for idempotent GETs in `fetch_image`; emit a one-line `log::info!(target: "images", route = engine|cdn|hosted)` per resolution and surface a counter in `suwayomi_status`; expose an `imageMode`/`nativeEngine` runtime override in localStorage so device verification can flip paths without a rebuild.

findings.title: Zero automated coverage of NativeImageProvider's branch selection — the single most load-bearing routing decision in the lane
findings.detail: `NativeImageProvider.resolve` (image-provider.ts:213-225) picks between four byte paths (engine `/api/`, own-asset `/covers/`+`/avatars/`, MangaDex host, generic fallback) and nothing tests it. The only e2e artefacts are apps/reader/src-tauri/e2e/{native-read,fallback-ladder,offline-queue,android-jdk-probe}; native-read stubs `suwayomi_image`/`fetch_image` at the `invoke` boundary (e2e/native-read/tauri-core-stub.mjs:18-26) and drives `invoke` directly (e2e/native-read/harness.entry.ts:250) rather than going through the provider, and grep shows no `.test.ts`/`.check.ts` anywhere references `NativeImageProvider` or `WebImageProvider`. The Rust side does test `is_blocked_ip`/`validate_image_path` (lib.rs:283-359, suwayomi.rs:767-795) but nothing tests the JS classifier that decides which Rust command is called.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone changes the hosted cover URL shape (e.g. drops SUWAYOMI_PUBLIC_URL so paths become relative `/api/v1/manga/...`) and native silently starts routing hosted ids into the embedded engine via `isEnginePath` — every cover 404s from the local engine and no test fails. Same blind spot for a new own-asset prefix or a MangaDex host-pattern change.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a check under apps/reader/src-tauri/e2e/ (same pattern as fallback-ladder.check.ts) that shims `@tauri-apps/api/core` and asserts, for a table of representative URLs, exactly which command name and argument NativeImageProvider invokes — including a case pinning that no input ever yields a workerBaseUrl request.
